tasks.title: HANGS General Contracting · FY2026 Receivables Confirmations
tasks.description: Audit HANGS General Contracting LP’s contract receivables and retainage at June 30, 2026 from 7 Excel, PDF and Word files: the trial balance, the aging, the contract schedule, the audit team’s confirmation control log and the customers’ replies, the July and August receipts and the controller’s collection notes. Select customers by size and risk, send and receive confirmations, follow up the non-responses with receipts after the year end, reconcile every difference, test the retainage and the allowance. Produce formula-linked workpapers with tickmarks and a draft findings memo. The CPA reviews, decides every open item and concludes.
tasks.outputs: Two files: formula-linked Excel workpapers with tickmarks and evidence tabs, and a draft findings memo PDF for the CPA with evidence trails and the original files attached
tasks.outputsPath: Outputs/HANGS General Contracting FY2026 Receivables Audit
tasks.gates: Draft workpapers and findings memo, not reviewed, concluded or signed. Not an audit report and no opinion. Open items stay open. The CPA concludes.
tasks.periodLine: FY2026: receivables at June 30, 2026 · audit procedures and a draft findings memo for the CPA.

run.title: HANGS General Contracting · FY2026 Receivables Confirmations

lines.text: Pier Nine: its $1,957,000.00 check, dated June 29, was deposited on July 2, 2026. Cash in transit to HGC at the year end is still a receivable: no misstatement. Kestrel Point: HGC agreed the $28,600.00 credit in writing on June 18, 2026, before the year end, but recorded it in July; revenue and receivables are overstated by it (AR-01), and Kestrel paid $510,000.00, the rest. Brindlewood: the district paid $371,250.00 and keeps $41,250.00 of liquidated damages; HGC has asked for a time extension and recorded nothing. Whether HGC will collect it is a judgment (AR-02).

run.title: HANGS General Contracting · FY2026 Receivables Confirmations

lines.text: The client records no allowance and says every contract receivable has been collected except where a credit was agreed (N4). Corliss Medical Group’s $186,935.00 is the exception: it disputes the change order work in the final billing, did not answer the confirmation or three letters, has paid nothing since December, and HGC has filed a lien. The job itself finished at a loss (the job schedule testing’s LOSS-01). A specific allowance of up to $186,935.00 is a judgment for the CPA (AR-03); a lien helps only if the clinic’s property covers it.

lines.text: Known misstatements add up to $28,600.00, 8.4% of the $340,000.00 materiality (AR-01). The judgments are larger: Brindlewood’s $41,250.00 (AR-02) and the Corliss allowance of up to $186,935.00 (AR-03). Recorded together with AR-01 they come to $256,785.00, more than the $255,000.00 performance materiality, so the CPA weighs them together and with the other FY2026 areas. Concluding is the CPA’s job; the machine stops here.

Three owners confirmed what they hold; Tideflats did not reply, but its $102,500.00 is 5% of the $2,050,000.00 its pay applications billed, and it paid the June billing net of it. Retainage on the jobs completed in the year has been billed for release and sits in contract receivables, where Brindlewood’s difference arose.

events.result: The client records no allowance and says every contract receivable has been collected except where a credit was agreed (N4). Corliss Medical Group’s $186,935.00 is the exception: it disputes the change order work in the final billing, did not answer the confirmation or three letters, has paid nothing since December, and HGC has filed a lien. The job itself finished at a loss (the job schedule testing’s LOSS-01). A specific allowance of up to $186,935.00 is a judgment for the CPA (AR-03); a lien helps only if the clinic’s property covers it.

Add up what was found and set it against materiality

Known misstatements add up to $28,600.00, 8.4% of the $340,000.00 materiality (AR-01). The judgments are larger: Brindlewood’s $41,250.00 (AR-02) and the Corliss allowance of up to $186,935.00 (AR-03). Recorded together with AR-01 they come to $256,785.00, more than the $255,000.00 performance materiality, so the CPA weighs them together and with the other FY2026 areas. Concluding is the CPA’s job; the machine stops here.
